questions.question: Let $\boldsymbol{A}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ and $\boldsymbol{b}\in\mathbb{R}^{m}$, and let (a) be the system $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$. Farkas' lemma says that exactly one of (a) and a second system (b) in $\boldsymbol{y}\in\mathbb{R}^m$ has a solution. Which system is (b)?
options: $\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ and $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\leq0$
$\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ and $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}<0$
$\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\leq\boldsymbol{0}$ and $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}<0$
$\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, $\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ and $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}<0$

questions.question: Let $\boldsymbol{A}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ and $\boldsymbol{b}\in\mathbb{R}^{m}$, with columns $\boldsymbol{A}_1,\dots,\boldsymbol{A}_n$. Which geometric condition on $\boldsymbol{b}$ is equivalent to the system $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$ having a solution with $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$?
options: $\boldsymbol{b}$ lies in the linear span of $\boldsymbol{A}_1,\dots,\boldsymbol{A}_n$
$\boldsymbol{b}$ lies in the convex hull of $\boldsymbol{A}_1,\dots,\boldsymbol{A}_n$
$\boldsymbol{b}$ lies in the cone generated by $\boldsymbol{A}_1,\dots,\boldsymbol{A}_n$
$\boldsymbol{b}$ lies in the cone generated by the rows of $\boldsymbol{A}$

questions.question: Let $\boldsymbol{A}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ and $\boldsymbol{b}\in\mathbb{R}^{m}$. Suppose $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ satisfies $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$ and $\boldsymbol{y}\in\mathbb{R}^m$ satisfies $\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$. Which argument shows that then $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}<0$ is impossible?
options: $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}=\boldsymbol{x}^{\top}(\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y})$, a sum of products of nonnegative numbers, so $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq0$

$\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ forces $\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, and $\boldsymbol{b}=\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, so $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq0$
$\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}=-\lVert\boldsymbol{y}\rVert^2$ for the nearest-point choice of $\boldsymbol{y}$, which is never positive
$\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}=\boldsymbol{x}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}$, and both $\boldsymbol{x}$ and $\boldsymbol{y}$ are nonnegative, so $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq0$

questions.question: Let $\boldsymbol{A}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ and $\boldsymbol{b}\in\mathbb{R}^{m}$ with $\boldsymbol{b}=\boldsymbol{0}$. Which conclusion does Farkas' lemma give for the systems (a) $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ and (b) $\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}<0$?
options: (b) holds with $\boldsymbol{y}=\boldsymbol{0}$, since $\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{0}=\boldsymbol{0}$ satisfies $\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$
(a) holds only if $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{0}$ has a solution $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ with $\boldsymbol{x}\neq\boldsymbol{0}$
Which one holds depends on $\boldsymbol{A}$: (b) holds if some column of $\boldsymbol{A}$ is negative
(a) holds with $\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{0}$, and (b) fails since $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}=0$ for every $\boldsymbol{y}$

questions.question: Some books state the second alternative of Farkas' lemma for $\boldsymbol{A}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$, $\boldsymbol{b}\in\mathbb{R}^m$ as: some $\boldsymbol{z}$ has $\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{z}\leq\boldsymbol{0}$ and $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{z}>0$. How does this relate to the system $\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}<0$?
options: The two are negations, so the version with $\boldsymbol{z}$ holds exactly when $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ does
The version with $\boldsymbol{z}$ is the variant for $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$ with $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$
$\boldsymbol{z}$ solves one system exactly when $\boldsymbol{y}=-\boldsymbol{z}$ solves the other
They agree only when $\boldsymbol{A}$ is square and invertible, so that $\boldsymbol{z}=-\boldsymbol{y}$ is unique

questions.question: Let $\boldsymbol{A}$ have columns $(2,-1)$ and $(1,1)$, let $\boldsymbol{b}=(-1,2)$ and $\boldsymbol{y}=(1,-1)$. Which conclusion follows from computing $\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}$ and $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}$ and applying Farkas' lemma?
options: $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$ has no nonnegative solution, as $\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}=(3,0)$ and $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}=-3$
Nothing follows, as a certificate must satisfy $\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, but here $y_2=-1$
$\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$ has no solution of any sign, as $\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}=(3,0)$ and $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}=-3$
Nothing follows, as $\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}=(3,0)$ has a zero entry and the test needs every entry positive

questions.question: Let $\boldsymbol{A}$ have columns $(2,1)$ and $(-1,1)$. For which right-hand side $\boldsymbol{b}$ does $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$ have a solution with $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, so that the alternative $\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}<0$ has none?
options: $\boldsymbol{b}=(3,0)$
$\boldsymbol{b}=(-4,-2)$
$\boldsymbol{b}=(0,-3)$
$\boldsymbol{b}=(1,2)$

questions.question: The system $x_1-2x_2\leq-4$, $x_2\leq1$, $x_1,x_2\geq0$ has no solution. Which $\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ certifies this through the variant of Farkas' lemma, that is, $\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ and $\boldsymbol{y}^{\top}\boldsymbol{b}<0$ with $\boldsymbol{A}$ and $\boldsymbol{b}$ read off from the inequalities?
options: $\boldsymbol{y}=(1,1)$
$\boldsymbol{y}=(1,2)$
$\boldsymbol{y}=(1,4)$
$\boldsymbol{y}=(0,1)$

questions.question: Let $\boldsymbol{A}=(2\ \ 5\ \ 0)$, a $1\times3$ matrix (so $m=1$), and $b=-3$. Which statement about the systems (a) $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}=b$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ and (b) $\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}y\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, $by<0$ with $y\in\mathbb{R}$ is correct?
options: (b) holds with $y=-1$, the sign that matches $b=-3$
(a) holds with $\boldsymbol{x}=(-\tfrac{3}{2},0,0)$, since $2\cdot(-\tfrac{3}{2})=-3$
(b) holds with $y=1$: $\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}y=(2,5,0)$ and $by=-3$
(a) holds, since the zero column leaves $x_3$ free to fit $b$

questions.question: Consider the system $x_1+2x_2\leq2$, $-2x_1-x_2\leq-5$, $x_1,x_2\geq0$, with $\boldsymbol{A}$ and $\boldsymbol{b}$ read off from the inequalities. A student notes that $\boldsymbol{y}=(1,0)$ has $\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, $\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}=(1,2)\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ and $\boldsymbol{y}^{\top}\boldsymbol{b}=2\geq0$. Which conclusion is correct?
options: The system is feasible, as this $\boldsymbol{y}=(1,0)$ shows by the variant of Farkas' lemma
The system is infeasible, as $\boldsymbol{y}=(2,1)$ shows by the variant of Farkas' lemma
The system is infeasible, since $\boldsymbol{y}=(0,1)$ has $\boldsymbol{y}^{\top}\boldsymbol{b}=-5<0$
The system is feasible, as $\boldsymbol{x}=(2,0)$ shows by direct substitution

questions.question: In Farkas' lemma for $\boldsymbol{A}$ and $\boldsymbol{b}$, the strict inequality $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}<0$ (with $\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$) is replaced by $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\leq0$. What happens to the claim that exactly one of this system and $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ is solvable?
options: It fails only for $\boldsymbol{b}$ on the boundary of the cone, where some $\boldsymbol{y}\neq\boldsymbol{0}$ has $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}=0$
It still holds, since the weakened system is solvable exactly when $\boldsymbol{b}$ lies outside the cone

It still holds once $\boldsymbol{y}\neq\boldsymbol{0}$ is required, since $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}=0$ then cannot occur together with $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$
It fails: $\boldsymbol{y}=\boldsymbol{0}$ solves the weakened system, so both hold whenever $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ does

questions.question: Let $\boldsymbol{A}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ and $K=\{\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\colon\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$. In the proof that $\boldsymbol{b}\notin K$ implies a solution of $\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}<0$, where is it used that $K$ is closed?
options: It guarantees a point $\boldsymbol{q}\in K$ nearest to $\boldsymbol{b}$, from which $\boldsymbol{y}=\boldsymbol{q}-\boldsymbol{b}$ is built
It shows that $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$ and $\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}<0$ cannot both have solutions
It makes the separating hyperplane pass through $\boldsymbol{0}$, which gives $(\boldsymbol{q}-\boldsymbol{b})^{\top}\boldsymbol{q}=0$
It makes the solution $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ of $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{q}$ unique, so that $\boldsymbol{y}$ is well defined

questions.question: Farkas' lemma for $[\boldsymbol{A}\ \ \boldsymbol{I}_m](\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{s})=\boldsymbol{b}$, $(\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{s})\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, with a slack vector $\boldsymbol{s}$, gives the variant for $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$. Where does the sign condition $\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ in the variant come from?
options: It is a convention added by hand: the equation version also holds with $\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ required
From the columns of $\boldsymbol{A}$, whose condition $\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ forces $\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$
From the slack columns: $[\boldsymbol{A}\ \ \boldsymbol{I}_m]^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ contains $\boldsymbol{I}_m\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$
From $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, whose sign carries over to $\boldsymbol{y}$ in the second system

questions.question: Let $\boldsymbol{A}$ have columns $(1,2)$ and $(0,1)$, so $K=\{\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\colon\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$, and let $\boldsymbol{b}=(3,1)\notin K$. The proof of Farkas' lemma takes the nearest point $\boldsymbol{q}\in K$ to $\boldsymbol{b}$ and $\boldsymbol{y}=\boldsymbol{q}-\boldsymbol{b}$. Which pair is it?
options: $\boldsymbol{q}=(1,2)$ and $\boldsymbol{y}=(2,-1)$
$\boldsymbol{q}=(1,2)$ and $\boldsymbol{y}=(-2,1)$
$\boldsymbol{q}=(0,1)$ and $\boldsymbol{y}=(-3,0)$
$\boldsymbol{q}=(3,6)$ and $\boldsymbol{y}=(0,5)$

questions.question: Let $\boldsymbol{A}$ have columns $(1,1)$ and $(1,-1)$, and $\boldsymbol{b}=(t,3)$ with $t\in\mathbb{R}$. For exactly which $t$ does $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$ have a solution $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, so that no $\boldsymbol{y}$ with $\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}<0$ exists?
options: $t\geq-3$
$-3\leq t\leq3$
$t\geq3$

questions.question: Let $\boldsymbol{A}$ have columns $(1,0,1)$ and $(0,1,1)$, and $\boldsymbol{b}=(1,1,1)$; the system $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$ has no solution at all. Which $\boldsymbol{y}$ satisfies Farkas' second system $\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}<0$?
options: $\boldsymbol{y}=(-1,-1,1)$
$\boldsymbol{y}=(1,1,-1)$
$\boldsymbol{y}=(0,0,-1)$
$\boldsymbol{y}=(-1,-1,2)$

questions.question: Let $C=\{(u,v)\colon v>0\}\cup\{(u,0)\colon u\geq0\}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^2$ and $\boldsymbol{p}=(-1,0)\notin C$. Every $\boldsymbol{y}$ with $\boldsymbol{y}^{\top}\boldsymbol{v}\geq0$ for all $\boldsymbol{v}\in C$ has $\boldsymbol{p}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}=0$, so no such $\boldsymbol{y}$ has $\boldsymbol{p}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}<0$. Why does this not contradict Farkas' lemma?
options: $\boldsymbol{p}$ is a boundary point of $C$, and Farkas' lemma excludes boundary points
$C$ is not convex, and Farkas' lemma needs the cone of the columns to be convex
$C$ is not a cone, since it contains the vector $(1,0)$ but not the vector $(-1,0)$
$C$ is not closed, hence not of the form $\{\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\colon\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$

questions.question: The system $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$ has a solution of any sign if and only if $[\boldsymbol{A}\ \ -\boldsymbol{A}]\boldsymbol{w}=\boldsymbol{b}$ has one with $\boldsymbol{w}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$. By Farkas' lemma for $[\boldsymbol{A}\ \ -\boldsymbol{A}]$, which system in $\boldsymbol{y}$ is solvable exactly when $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$ is not?
options: $\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ and $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}<0$
$\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}=\boldsymbol{0}$ and $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}<0$
$\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, $\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}=\boldsymbol{0}$ and $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}<0$
$\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\leq\boldsymbol{0}$ and $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}<0$

questions.question: Let $\boldsymbol{A}$ have columns $(1,2)$ and $(2,1)$; the polar cone of $K=\{\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\colon\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}\}$ is $K^{\circ}=\operatorname{Cone}(\{(-2,1),(1,-2)\})$. For $\boldsymbol{b}=(1,3)$, which statement about (a) $\boldsymbol{b}\in K$ and (b) $\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}<0$ is correct?
options: (a) holds, since $\boldsymbol{b}$ has a positive inner product with both columns
(a) holds, since $(1,-2)^{\top}\boldsymbol{b}=-5\leq0$
(b) holds with $\boldsymbol{y}=(2,-1)$
(b) holds with $\boldsymbol{y}=(-2,1)$

questions.question: Let $\boldsymbol{A}$ have columns $(2,-1)$, $(-1,1)$, $(1,1)$ and $\boldsymbol{b}=(0,3)$. Setting $x_2=0$ in $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$ gives $\boldsymbol{x}=(-1,0,2)$. What follows for (a) $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ and (b) $\boldsymbol{A}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}<0$?
options: (a) holds, for example with $\boldsymbol{x}=(1,3,1)\geq\boldsymbol{0}$
(b) holds, since the solution $\boldsymbol{x}=(-1,0,2)$ has a negative entry
(b) holds with $\boldsymbol{y}=(1,-1)$, since $\boldsymbol{b}^{\top}\boldsymbol{y}=-3<0$
(a) holds, and $\boldsymbol{x}=(0,\frac{3}{2},\frac{3}{2})$ is its only solution with $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$
